stories.headline: Jaishankar urges Commonwealth partners to 'de-risk and diversify'
stories.deck: S. Jaishankar said Commonwealth partners need to make more efforts to enhance local distribution, adding that more connectivity corridors are good for business
stories.bodyText:
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar has urged Commonwealth partners to "de-risk and diversify", emphasising the need to enhance local distribution among member nations.
Mr. Jaishankar arrived in St. John's on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) to attend the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM).
"Commonwealth partners also need to de-risk and diversify. This requires shorter and trusted supply chains," Mr. Jaishankar posted on social media after attending the Commonwealth heads of government and business leaders' breakfast meeting on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).
Mr. Jaishankar said Commonwealth partners need to make more efforts to enhance local distribution, adding that more connectivity corridors are good for business.
"Promote training and capacity building as it gives more options for partners," he said.
EAM said that the Indian business community spread across the world is an asset for the Commonwealth.
Speaking about the significance of digital public infrastructure for good governance, Mr. Jaishankar said, "Digital is a game changer as it promotes efficiency, good governance and growth."
"International Solar Alliance and the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure can be leveraged for climate action," Mr. Jaishankar said.
Sharing India's experiences in Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR), Mr. Jaishankar said, "Our First Responder experiences and HADR activities suggest the need for local hubs."
He said that comfort within the Commonwealth nations "can build business for growth and prosperity", adding that mobility of skills can be an important Commonwealth focus.
The theme of this year's CHOGM is accelerating partnerships and investment for a prosperous Commonwealth.
Mr. Jaishankar also met with the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, Andy Burnham and the Prime Minister of Australia, Anthony Albanese, on the sidelines of CHOGM.
He discussed the India–U.K. Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) with the U.K. PM Burnham.
"Discussed strengthening our economic partnership in the context of CETA, as well as the global landscape," Mr. Jaishankar posted on social media after meeting with Burnham.

stories.headline: 'Shawarma law' not 'Sharia law': Abdul El-Sayed's remark goes viral after senate win
stories.bodyText:
The US midterm elections have delivered a major victory for Democrats, with the party making significant gains across the country and flipping control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate.
Among the notable victories was that of Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, whose remarks about implementing "shawarma law" instead of "Sharia law" have gone viral on social media.
El-Sayed, 42, an epidemiologist and former public health official aligned with the Democratic Party's progressive wing, defeated Republican candidate and former representative Mike Rogers in one of the country's closely watched Senate races, NBC News projected. His victory makes him the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.
In his victory speech, El-Sayed introduced himself by his full name, Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed, before using Arabic expressions to take a swipe at Republicans and Vice-President JD Vance.
“My name is Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed,” he said, before explaining his repeated use of the Arabic expression "inshallah", meaning "God willing", during the campaign.
“Up until right about now, you might have noticed I always say “inshallah”, or “God willing”, whenever the outcome of this race was mentioned. But today, tonight, we can turn that inshallah into alhamdulillah. For the rightwing ops, that just means “praise be to God,” OK?”
He continued his remarks with a reference to Vance, saying, “JD, habibi, there is this delicious irony in the fact that you’re constitutionally obligated to swear me in in January.”
El-Sayed also used his speech to criticise US support for Israel and speak about the situation in Gaza, condemning the abuse faced by those who have raised concerns about the conflict.
“See, they try to call you hateful if you believe that Palestinian kids should get to grow up in the land of their forefathers without being murdered by our tax dollars,” he said.
“Michiganders, we want our taxes spent here, for schools here, and healthcare here, and infrastructure here. We don’t want our money sent to do apartheid or genocide or war.”
El-Sayed's victory came despite a campaign marked by Islamophobic attacks from President Donald Trump and other Republicans. Trump had called him a “communist” and described him as a “jihadist” and a member of the Egyptian Muslim Brotherhood.
He also faced a setback in the final days of the campaign when Democratic Representative Haley Stevens, whom he had defeated in the party's primary, withdrew her support and endorsed Rogers after attending church with the Republican candidate.
El-Sayed had defeated Stevens to secure the Democratic nomination earlier this year, challenging the party establishment with a campaign centred on progressive policies. He advocated for universal healthcare through the Medicare for All proposal and called for an end to US military aid to Israel.
Republicans had portrayed the general election as a referendum on the Democratic Party's progressive wing, making the contest between El-Sayed and Rogers one of the most closely watched Senate races in the country.
His win also extends the Republican Party's long-running electoral drought in Michigan. Republicans have not won a Senate seat in the state since 1994. El-Sayed will succeed retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters.
His victory was among several electoral breakthroughs for women, candidates of colour and other underrepresented groups in Tuesday's elections. Democrats made significant gains in key statewide races and flipped control of both chambers of Congress, riding a wave of dissatisfaction with the Trump administration.
The results also pointed to gains for Democrats in traditionally conservative states, with analysts, civil rights leaders and grassroots voter organisations suggesting that the party had attracted Republican voters while rebuilding support among its traditional constituencies.
Black and Latino voters, in particular, had emerged as increasingly contested groups in recent election cycles, as the latest results reshaped the political landscape and expanded representation in the highest levels of American government.

briefs.headline: Donald Trump’s midterm defeat dims hopes of North Korea meeting
briefs.deck: Mr. Kim’s powerful sister Kim Yo Jong signalled that there was little appetite for renewed dialogue with Washington, saying Pyongyang had “no need to sit face to face with such unreliable and hostile persons”
briefs.bodyText:
A meeting between Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un appears increasingly unlikely when the U.S. president travels to Asia in November, analysts say, after he suffered a crushing midterm election defeat.
Mr. Trump had said he “may” meet Mr. Kim this month and that it “would be exciting”, but appeared to backtrack in October, saying, “I don’t know... I’m not sure that anybody’s asking for a meeting,” while adding that his “relationship with Kim Jong Un is very good.”
Mr. Trump’s focus on Mr. Kim and his scaling back of joint U.S.-South Korean military drills have alarmed Asian allies, while sparking speculation that he is seeking a foreign policy win as his war with Iran stalls.
But Mr. Kim’s powerful sister Kim Yo Jong signalled on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that there was little appetite for renewed dialogue with Washington, saying Pyongyang had “no need to sit face to face with such unreliable and hostile persons”.
“The choice for peace includes dialogue of course, but this is not surely equated with national interests for us,” she said.
Ms. Kim Yo Jong’s comments came after the FBI accused North Korea of a $6 billion heist from cryptocurrency exchange Binance — allegations she had previously slammed as “a grave political provocation”.
Ms. Kim’s statement marked “a shift from defence to offence”, said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University’s Institute for Far Eastern Studies in South Korea.
“The latest statement uses the (cyberattack) issue as an opportunity to condemn the entire US policy of pressure against North Korea,” he told AFP.
In 2019, North Korea’s Kim Jong Un made a 60-hour train journey home from Hanoi empty-handed after a summit with Trump collapsed.
Now, the dynamic has reversed. Trump is making repeated overtures, only to be met with reluctance from Pyongyang.
“For Kim Jong Un, maintaining the status quo is the best option right now,” Lim said.
Weakened Trump
Analysts say the North Korean leader has even less incentive to meet Trump after his Republican party suffered a thumping defeat in the U.S. midterm elections on November 3.
Voters handed control of Congress to the Democrats in a stunning rebuke to Mr. Trump, leaving him as a lame duck President for the remaining two years of his term.
“Trump is expected to continue pursuing top-down dialogue with North Korea”, said Yang Moo-jin, former president of the South’s University of North Korean Studies.
But Washington’s “divided government and Trump’s lame-duck status will be an important variable for North Korea”.
Pyongyang will be sceptical of Washington’s ability to deliver lasting concessions, said Michael Bosack, founding director of the Parley Policy Institute and a former UN Command official.
“The Kim regime is looking for substantial and durable changes in US policy towards North Korea. Right now, nothing Trump offers comes with a guarantee that it will last beyond January 2029,” Bosack told AFP, referring to the date when the US president’s second term ends.
Mr. Kim’s deepening ties with Russia and China have also strengthened his position and reduced his incentive to engage with Washington.
North Korea’s economy grew more than three percent for a third straight year in 2025, Seoul’s central bank estimated in July, citing Pyongyang’s “expansion of economic cooperation with Russia” as its major driver.
Nuclear ambitions
Even if Mr. Trump and Mr. Kim agree to meet, their differences over North Korea’s nuclear weapons programme remain a major obstacle to any breakthrough.
Pyongyang has repeatedly made clear it is no longer prepared to discuss denuclearisation.
Kim Yo Jong said in September that the country’s nuclear-armed status was “absolute”, calling those hoping for denuclearisation “idiots”.
It came as South Korea’s dovish President Lee Jae Myung -- who has repeatedly offered Pyongyang talks without preconditions — suggested Washington seek a freeze, rather than the immediate elimination, of the North’s nuclear programme and offer sanctions relief in return.
That approach would face significant obstacles following Trump’s midterm defeat though, with Democrats committed to denuclearisation and Congress holding powers over sanctions relief.
“Pyongyang retains negative memories of failing to make progress in negotiations under the Biden administration because of its position that there would be no sanctions relief or dialogue without prior denuclearisation measures,” Kyungnam University’s Lim said.
North Korea’s distrust of Washington, coupled with the uncertainty surrounding any agreement with Trump, could boost its nuclear ambitions.
“North Korea’s belief that independently advancing its nuclear arsenal, regardless of changes in US administrations or political parties, was the right and strategically sound decision will be further reinforced,” Lim said.
Pyongyang has carried out a flurry of weapons tests in recent weeks, including trials of cluster-bomb warheads, attack drones, a precision-guided torpedo system and an intermediate-range hypersonic missile.
“The development, testing and training of new weapons will become regular and routine activities,” Lim predicted.

briefs.headline: What the U.S. midterms mean for ties with China
briefs.deck: Here is how the outcome of the vote, which offers the Democratic Party the power to stymie President Donald Trump’s maverick foreign policy, could impact the thorny relationship between Washington and Beijing
briefs.bodyText:
A sweeping victory for Democrats in U.S. midterm elections this week, giving them control of Congress, presents both an opportunity and challenge for top rival China, analysts say.
Here is how the outcome of the vote, which offers the Democratic Party the power to stymie President Donald Trump’s maverick foreign policy, could impact the thorny relationship between Washington and Beijing:
Will tariffs be limited?
Winning control of both houses in the U.S. Congress puts Democrats in a position to limit Mr. Trump’s liberal use of tariffs on Chinese products in the two years he has left in office, analysts say.
That could be a potential blow to Mr. Trump, who has wielded duties throughout a frenzied US-China trade war before the two sides reached a truce, set to expire in January.
If Democrats limit Mr. Trump, that means he “will be less able to leverage a tariff card in negotiations with China”, said Wu Xinbo, dean at the Institute of International Studies at Fudan University in Shanghai.
However, Democrats will also have to weigh their actions against the popularity of Mr. Trump’s tariffs among U.S. businesses.
Congress will “take every opportunity to thwart (Mr. Trump’s policies) over the next two years”, said Drew Thompson, a senior fellow at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies at Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University.
But Democrats will still have to tread carefully on further restricting tariffs that “are popular with unions, blue-collar workers and small businesses... who have historically been a base constituency for the Democrats”, Mr. Thompson said.
Congress will be “less inclined to support measures that would sharply escalate pressure on China if doing so risks raising costs for American consumers and businesses or increasing the likelihood of conflict”, said Patricia Kim, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution in Washington.
Taiwan a ‘game changer’?
The issue of Taiwan, the U.S.-backed democratic island claimed by Beijing, could be a “game changer”, said Neil Shearing, group chief economist at Capital Economics.
Washington is Taipei’s most important security backer and has sold billions of dollars’ worth of arms to Taiwan that the island would use to fend off a potential Chinese attack.
But Mr. Trump threw the U.S. stance into question in May when he declared that U.S. arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip in talks with China. His administration has since delayed for months a $14-billion batch of weapons.
China could use the remaining two years of Mr. Trump’s presidency to increase pressure on Taiwan, particularly if Beijing “judges that Washington is distracted or that Trump would be willing to agree terms to not intervene”, Shearing wrote in a note.
Mr. Trump, who recently hailed his “great friendship” with China’s President Xi Jinping, has so far resisted political pressure from Democrats — and some Republican lawmakers — to greenlight the arms package.
But a Democrat-controlled Congress “may force Trump to resume arms sales to Taiwan next year”, Wu said.
“If that happens, that will also undermine the stability of U.S.-China relationship.”
Alternatively, for China, renewed support of Taipei from the U.S. Congress may be “a stronger incentive for (Beijing) to play it safer with Taiwan”, said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute.
Nevertheless, Thompson pointed out, while Congress can pass bills requiring Mr. Trump to approve an arms sale, the president retains the power to veto it “or simply ignore it”.
Will Beijing treat Trump as a lame duck?
From China’s perspective, even though Mr. Trump has been politically weakened by the midterms, Beijing is unlikely to change its strategy towards working with him, analysts say.
“Beijing is likely to continue cultivating him through high-profile, leader-to-leader engagement with Xi Jinping, viewing this as the least costly way to manage relations with Washington,” said Kim.
“Neither Beijing nor Washington appears to expect or seek a fundamental improvement in bilateral relations,” she added.
Tsang of the SOAS China Institute said “Trump being relegated to lame-duck status will be used by the Chinese to put more pressure on him”.
But, he added, Beijing is “calculating” and “would not want to push too hard and trigger Trump behaving totally irresponsibly”.

briefs.headline: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed claims victory in Michigan Senate battle
briefs.deck: El-Sayed won despite a last-minute hiccup in his campaign when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary, came out in support of Rogers at the 11th hour
briefs.bodyText:
Democrat Abdul El-Sayed said early on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that he had won a US Senate seat in Michigan over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, which would make him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress.
“Michigan, we did it!” Mr. El-Sayed said in a speech at his election headquarters in Detroit.
“I am so proud and honored to stand here as your senator-elect from the great state of Michigan.”
Mr. El-Sayed won despite a last-minute hiccup in his campaign when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, came out in support of Rogers at the 11th hour.
The Michigan doctor rallied voters on leftist campaign promises, including universal health care, to hold a key U.S. Senate seat for Democrats, taking over from the retiring Gary Peters.
Republicans ran a scorched-earth campaign to paint Democrats as communists and branded Mr. El-Sayed a terrorist who would endanger Americans.
But the straight-talking 42-year-old El-Sayed pledged to help cash-strapped voters navigate America’s thorny health care system.
“You deserve to be able to see a doctor without getting a huge bill,” he told Michiganders on the eve of the vote, vowing to upend America’s divisive multi-billion-dollar for-profit medical system.
During the race, Mr. El-Sayed drew huge campaign crowds across the state, even in deeply conservative Republican areas.
Mr. El-Sayed also vowed to get “money out of politics” and address the harsh economic woes that have voters yearning for a political newcomer to shake up the status quo.
The election makes Mr. El-Sayed the first Democratic doctor in the Senate since 1969.

briefs.headline: U.S. Midterm election Democrats win five governor races as Hinojosa, Bottoms, Haaland make history
briefs.deck: Hinojosa becomes Texas’s first Latina governor, Bottoms the first Black woman elected governor in the US, and Haaland the first Native American woman to lead a state
briefs.bodyText:
Democrats are on track for big gains in governor races, notching victories in Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Georgia and Wisconsin, according to U.S. media projections, with a number of other races still too early to call as of early Wednesday (November 4, 2026).
Three candidates made history. In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms became the country’s first Black woman elected governor. In Texas, Democrat Gina Hinojosa became the first Latina governor in the state’s history, unseating a well-financed Republican incumbent in a historically conservative state. And in New Mexico, Democrat Deb Haaland became the country’s first female Native American governor.
A total of three dozen governor races were on the ballot in the elections, with President Donald Trump’s unpopularity and the cost of living at the top of voters’ minds, alongside local concerns ranging from water rights and data centres to cancer rates.
If Democrats can manage a net gain of at least two seats, they will lead a majority of states for the first time since 2010.
Here are eight key governor races.
Gina Hinojosa becomes state’s first Latina governor in Texas
Ms. Hinojosa, a Texas state representative, defeated Texas Governor Greg Abbott to become the first Democrat to be elected governor since 1990. She also became the first Latina governor in the state’s history.
Ms. Hinojosa emerged as an unexpected competitor to one of the best-known and best-funded Republican governors in the country. Mr. Abbott outspent her nearly 8-1, according to The Texas Tribune.
Democrats initially wrote off the Texas governor’s race and struggled to find a candidate willing to run against Mr. Abbott.
Keisha Lance Bottoms becomes first Black woman elected governor in U.S.
Ms. Bottoms, the former Atlanta mayor, beat Republican Rick Jackson, a billionaire healthcare executive, in the race to succeed Republican Governor Brian Kemp. In doing so, she became the first Black woman elected governor in the U.S. and the first Democrat elected governor of Georgia in more than a quarter century.
Both parties viewed the gubernatorial race as an early test of voter sentiment in a state that will likely be a key presidential battleground in 2028.
Mr. Jackson, who spent more than $100 million of his own money on the race, generally aligned himself with Mr. Trump’s agenda, while Ms. Bottoms sought to mobilise the diverse Democratic coalition that helped Joe Biden win the state in 2020.
Ms. Bottoms rose to national prominence in 2020 as she guided Georgia’s largest city through protests, civil unrest and the COVID-19 pandemic. Her base is in the Atlanta metro area, whose rapid growth has reshaped Georgia politics.
Amy Acton defeats Vivek Ramaswamy after a contentious campaign in Ohio
Democrat Amy Acton, a physician, defeated Republican entrepreneur Vivek Ramaswamy after a race that drew national attention over an explosive attack ad featuring Ms. Acton’s estranged mother. In a video run by the Ramaswamy campaign, Donna Arthur disputed Ms. Acton’s account of a childhood marked by homelessness and sexual abuse and urged Ohioans not to vote for her.
Ms. Acton, a former director of the Ohio Department of Health who led the state’s response to the COVID-19 pandemic, has said she was sexually abused by her stepfather. The stepfather, who died in 2004, fled the state after he was charged with raping his stepdaughter and never stood trial.
The state’s reputation as a perennial swing state faded after 2016, when Mr. Trump won it with strong support from working-class voters, who helped to turn it into a reliably Republican state. Democrats have won just one of the state’s last nine gubernatorial elections.
Rob Sand wins first open governor’s race since 2006 in Iowa
State Auditor Rob Sand, the only Iowa Democrat currently holding statewide elected office, beat Republican businessman Zach Lahn in the state’s first open governor’s race since 2006. Incumbent Republican Governor Kim Reynolds did not seek re-election.
The state’s incidence of cancer, at the second-highest rate in the country behind Kentucky, emerged as a major campaign topic alongside kitchen-table issues such as the cost of living. Interest was fuelled by worries that exposure to nitrates, pesticides and other environmental contaminants may be contributing to the high cancer rate.
The race also focused on education and government accountability. Mr. Sand campaigned as an independent watchdog critical of Republican fiscal management and the state’s private-school voucher programme. Mr. Lahn embraced lower taxes, school choice and a more conservative approach to social issues.
David Crowley defeats Trump-endorsed Tom Tiffany in Wisconsin
A central question in Wisconsin’s gubernatorial race has been whether voters, who backed Mr. Trump in 2024 and Mr. Biden in 2020, want a governor aligned with the Republican president. Republican Tom Tiffany, a three-term U.S. representative endorsed by Mr. Trump, has played down that connection. But his Democratic opponent, Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, won the race after seeking to link Mr. Tiffany to Mr. Trump’s agenda.
In Congress, Mr. Tiffany has supported conservative causes such as gun rights and lower taxes, and co-sponsored federal legislation that would have banned most abortions after about six weeks of pregnancy. Mr. Crowley campaigned on support for abortion rights. Wisconsin bans abortion after 20 weeks and requires a 24-hour waiting period as well as parental consent for minors.
Democrat Aaron Ford trumps Joe Lombardo in tight race
Democrat Aaron Ford won the election as Governor of Nevada, defeating Republican incumbent Joe Lombardo.
Mr. Ford, the attorney general, defeated the incumbent Mr. Lombardo in what was considered one of the country’s most competitive governor’s races.
Mr. Ford ran with the backing of the Democratic congressional delegation, California Gov. Gavin Newsom and former Vice-President Kamala Harris.
All eyes on Arizona as race yet to be called in drought-hit state
Water has become a key campaign issue in drought-hit Arizona, where Democratic Governor Katie Hobbs is seeking re-election against Republican U.S. Representative Andy Biggs. Other top issues are the cost of living and immigration, with Ms. Hobbs seeking to position herself as tougher on border security than many national Democrats.
Mr. Biggs is a former head of the right-wing U.S. House Freedom Caucus, which has pushed for deep cuts in federal spending. Abortion rights have featured prominently in the race, with Ms. Hobbs a supporter while Mr. Biggs has a long record as an opponent. Arizona voters approved a constitutional amendment protecting abortion rights in 2024.
Democrat Jocelyn Benson and Republican John James battle for Michigan
Michigan’s race was one of the most competitive gubernatorial contests, pitting Democrat Jocelyn Benson, the state’s top election official, against Republican U.S. Representative John James. The candidates were battling to succeed term-limited Democratic Governor Gretchen Whitmer, making it one of 19 open-seat races this cycle.
Michigan is a closely divided swing state that Mr. Trump won in 2016 and 2024, while Mr. Biden carried it in 2020. Neither party has elected back-to-back governors in the state since the 1960s.

stories.headline: Olympic gold, Asiad medals stolen from hockey legend MM Somaya's Bengaluru home
stories.deck: MM Somaya, a hockey legend, faced a devastating burglary at his home in Bengaluru on October 28. The thieves stole valuables worth over Rs 3 lakh, including his Olympic gold medal. They used helmets during the break-in, targeting the house between 2.30am and 4am. Police have gathered CCTV footage and are optimistic about resolving the case soon.
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Last Wednesday, when hockey legend MM Somaya returned from his morning walk in Apangela, near his hometown Madikeri, his wife Shami greeted him with news of a burglary at their Bengaluru residence.
His first thoughts were about his most prized possessions - medals won for the country, including his gold medal from 1980 Moscow Olympics. He rushed back to find his worst fears confirmed. His house in HAL 3rd Stage had been broken into between 2.30am and 4am on Oct 28, and valuables worth over Rs 3 lakh, including four international medals, were stolen.
"I'm obviously very hurt because the medals are an irreplaceable symbol of years of dedication, sacrifice and service to the country," an anguished Somaya told TOI.
The two burglars, wearing helmets, also stole Rs 30,000 in cash and gold and silver articles. They entered after breaking open the main door and were captured on neighbours' CCTV cameras.
"Apart from the Olympic gold, two Asian Games medals - a silver from the 1982 Games in New Delhi and a bronze from the 1986 Games in Seoul - and a Champions Trophy bronze from 1982 were stolen," Somaya (67) added.
Neighbours alerted the couple around 7.30am, and they immediately left for Bengaluru. 
Police registered an FIR the same day and said they were confident of solving the case, citing strong clues.
"We have collected much CCTV footage from the area and have some vital clues on the miscreants. They had watched the house for some hours and, after ensuring it was locked, broke in. However, we will crack the case," an investigating officer said.
Somaya, a former India captain, moved to the city from Mumbai in 2025 after retiring from Bharat Petroleum.

stories.headline: Bengaluru woman returns ill-fitting clothes, searches online for e-commerce customer care number to claim Rs 441 refund, follows fraudster's instructions and loses Rs 1.05 lakh
stories.deck: Prema, a 49-year-old woman, lost Rs 1 lakh after contacting a scammer posing as customer care. She searched online for a refund number after returning clothes to an e-commerce site. Similarly, another homemaker, Soundarya, lost Rs 98,000 after reporting a damaged curd packet. Both victims made unauthorized transactions following interactions with individuals impersonating customer service. These…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: A Rs 441 refund query turned into a Rs 1-lakh nightmare for a 49-year-old woman, who lost money from two bank accounts after calling a number she mistook for an e-commerce company’s customer care helpline.
Homemaker Prema (name changed) told police she ordered clothes through an e-commerce site, but returned them as they did not fit her. The Horamavu resident requested a refund of Rs 441 a couple of weeks ago, which remained pending.
On October 31, she searched the internet and found the number 8893978138 listed as the company’s customer care number and spoke to a person, who identified himself as Tushar Singh.
The caller guided her through various steps to process the refund and asked her to click on a link and enter details.
As the process was taking a long time, her phone screen went blank and displayed a message asking her to wait for the refund.
Sensing something was wrong, Prema switched off her phone and removed her sim card.
However, when she switched on the phone again, she noticed unauthorised transactions from her bank accounts: Rs 90,000 had been withdrawn from one of her accounts and Rs 15,000 from another one.
The transactions took place between 11.14am and 11.17am on October 31. 
She told police Tushar Singh had siphoned off her money through a digital payment application.
Damaged curd packet leads to Rs 98,000 cyber fraud
In a separate incident in October, a 56-year-old homemaker lost Rs 98,000 to cyber fraud after ordering a packet of curd on Blinkit, finding it damaged and searching online for a customer care number to claim a refund.
She was allegedly duped after contacting fraudsters posing as customer care representatives and following a link they sent her on WhatsApp.
According to a complaint filed by Soundarya (name changed), a resident of an apartment on Palace Cross Road in Vasanth Nagar, she had ordered the curd on October 17. When the packet arrived in a damaged condition, she complained to the delivery agent, who advised her to contact customer care.

stories.headline: Karnataka will integrate all its skilling efforts into a single unified system: CM
stories.deck: To reshape State’s workforce pipeline, government will allocate ₹5,000 crore to streamline its fragmented skilling initiatives spread across various departments and entities and also train 30 lakh beneficiaries over the next seven years
stories.bodyText:
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has announced a plan to integrate the State’s fragmented skilling efforts into a single unified system, budgeting an estimated investment of ₹5,000 crore to train 30 lakh beneficiaries over the next seven years.
Speaking at the Bengaluru Skill Summit on Wednesday, the Chief Minister also revealed the formation of a new State Vision Group for skill development, chaired by Mindtree co-founder Subroto Bagchi, to fundamentally reshape the state’s workforce pipeline to meet future demands.
Shifting market demands
The policy shift comes at a time when Karnataka, which produces over one lakh engineering graduates every year, has several of them facing underemployment or accepting entry-level positions with low salaries. With over 550 Global Capability Centres (GCCs) currently operating in Bengaluru and an additional 500 targeted by 2029, the government is rushing to upgrade its vocational training ecosystem before an estimated 3.5 lakh upcoming jobs are introduced to the market.
Mr. Shivakumar stressed that traditional degrees were no longer the primary benchmark for corporate recruitment, drawing parallels to international markets where practical capability out-values formal certification.
The newly formed Vision Group would oversee the implementation of specialised training programmes across highly technical emerging sectors, including artificial intelligence, green energy, advanced manufacturing, and digital services. The initiative was aimed at capitalising on the State’s distinct demographic dividend, where 65% of the total population was under the age of 35, he added.
The summit witnessed the signing of more than 40 Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) involving local Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), which officials claim would immediately secure over 10,000 jobs for regional youth, anchoring the expanded training regime under the Koushalya Karnataka Yojane framework.
Udyoga Sethu launched
Mr. Shivakumar launched Udyoga Sethu, a digital employment platform by the State government at the Bengaluru Skill Summit to connect skilled talent with employment opportunities available with various enterprises.
Yuva Udyoga Setu is an AI-powered, unified skill development and employment portal and it serves as a direct bridge connecting local job seekers with verified private-sector employers. The platform, which operates under the Karnataka Skill Development Corporation (KSDC) and the Department of Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood, will offer seamless job matching (connects job seekers with corporate employers).
Enterprises can register and post their openings on the portal completely free of charge. It also claims to offer access to targeted training programs like the Chief Minister’s Kaushalya Karnataka Yojane (CMKKY) and specialised training for diverse segments (including Nal Jal Mitra and training for prison inmates).

stories.headline: After a decade, Chikkajala Fort near Bengaluru to get a new lease of life using CSR funds
stories.deck: In 2016, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), which implemented the road widening project of NH 44, demolished the northern side of the fort
stories.bodyText:
A decade after a part of it was demolished to make way for road works, the Chikkajala Fort, which is 25 km away from Bengaluru city and on the way to Kempegowda International Airport (KIA), will soon be restored using Corporate Social Responsbility (CSR) funds from a private organisation.
A ceremony was recently held at the fort to mark the beginning of the project, with Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda in attendance, along with members of Intach and Kashi Ra, the organisation funding the project.
The fort includes a small Anjaneya Swamy Temple, where a daily puja is performed by a local priest, and kalyani and stone mantapas on two acres under survey number 116, which falls under the jurisdiction of the Revenue Department. These were built in the 19th century, inspired by the Vijayanagara style, and used as a ‘chatra’ or rest stops for soldiers, businesspersons, and others professions who travelled long distances. The stones in the kalyani and mantapa feature carvings of nagabhanda, elephant, shivalinga, purnakumba and anjaneya, fishes, birds and a few others, said a senior official from the Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage.
When The Hindu visited Chikkajala Fort, huge trees and bushes had grown inside the mantapa. The branches and roots had spread across the roof and flooring of the mantapa while the stones of the kalyani and Anjaneya Temple are intact. However, there is no water in the kalyani, which has remained dry for a long time.
In 2016, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), which implemented the road widening project of NH 44, demolished the northern side (entrance) of the fort, which The Hindu had reported about then. The fort, which was circular in shape before the demolition, is now semi-circular and opens to the road.
Restoration plans
Meera Iyer, convener of the Bengaluru Chapter, Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH), said, “The villagers informed us that the bottom of the kalyani was cemented during a film shoot by the film team. Hence, there is no water in it. However, many trees have grown around and spread their roots in the mantapa. INTACH is yet to start its documentation and study on how to retain these trees and restore the stones of the mantapa. In our earlier projects, the trees were retained and walls were restored with the help of experts. After documentation, a Detailed Project Report (DPR) will be prepared, along with the calculation of the total cost it will incur.”
She added that once the fort is restored, it will be a tourist place for those visiting Bengaluru, and cultural activities are likely to be organised so that more people know the history and importance of the monument. “We are also planning to involve college students studying architecture and provide them with a first-hand experience working on live restoration projects like this fort,” she said.

briefs.headline: 'Why should men pay more': How Karnataka’s 33-35% BMTC fare hike will hit commuters and make intercity travel costlier
briefs.deck: Karnataka has announced substantial fare increases for its state-run transport corporations starting midnight. Commuters will face fare hikes between 23% and 35%, greatly impacting travel costs. Men, who already pay for rides while women travel free under the Shakti scheme, will be especially affected. The transport minister cited rising operational costs and fuel prices as reasons for the…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Adding to the season of hikes, Karnataka govt Wednesday delivered its hardest blow yet, announcing a steep fare revision across its four state-run transport corporations. BMTC fares will go up by 33% to 35% and those of 
KSRTC
, NWKRTC and KKRTC by 23% from Thursday midnight.
The shock value is the unprecedented scale of increase as fare revisions between 2009 and 2025 ranged between 3.5% and 15%.
With this, the base ticket price on BMTC is on par with that of Metro on certain routes, and rides on premier BMTC buses will hurt passengers more. Airport commuters, too, will have to spend more on Vayu Vajra services.
Citizens unleashed fury against the govt online, asking transport minister Byrathi Suresh the rationale behind the sharp hike: “How could men in Bengaluru bear a 35% hike when annual salary revision is barely 3%? Why is the Cong govt giving such atrocious Deepavali gifts to people? Why should men pay more to allow women to travel free?”
The minister defended the hike, citing operational costs, rising fuel prices and employee expenses, saying corporations were under severe financial stress. 
He denied suggestions that Shakti was hurting the corporation.
Intercity travel will burn a bigger hole. For instance, a journey from Bengaluru to Kalaburagi on an express bus service will now cost Rs 928 against Rs 754 earlier, an increase of Rs 174. Similarly, the Bengaluru-Belagavi fare has jumped from Rs 603 to Rs 742.
The hike is set to hit male commuters particularly hard. Of 1.25 crore passengers who use the four state-run transport corporations every day, 74.4 lakh are women travelling free under the Shakti scheme. This leaves more than 50 lakh passengers, largely men, paying for their rides.

briefs.headline: Karnataka bus fare hike: Byrathi Suresh blames rising diesel prices, cites ₹10,200 crore losses
briefs.deck: Fares on KSRTC, NWKRTC and KKRTC buses have increased by an average of 23%, while BMTC fares have gone up by 35%. The revised rates came into effect in the early hours of Thursday, November 5
briefs.bodyText:
Defending the Karnataka government’s decision to increase bus fares, Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh on Wednesday attributed the hike to repeated increases in diesel prices by the Union government, rising operational expenses and mounting financial losses.
Explaining the reasons behind the revision, the Minister said the Union government had increased diesel prices seven times since May, resulting in a cumulative increase of ₹10.47 per litre. The repeated fuel price hikes had significantly affected the financial position of the transport corporations, he said.
The four corporations spend nearly 80% of their revenue on diesel and staff-related expenses. Together, they spend approximately ₹15.60 crore every day on diesel, translating into an annual expenditure of ₹5,694 crore.
According to the Minister, the four corporations have collectively accumulated losses of approximately ₹10,200 crore.
Mr. Suresh pointed out that bus fares had been revised only once in the past 10 years, with a 15% increase implemented on January 5, 2025. However, the earlier revision had not been sufficient to offset the continuing rise in operational costs, he said.
He further said that the latest fare revision was necessary to prevent the corporations from slipping further into financial distress, although the increase would only partially help recover their accumulated losses.
‘Shakti not responsible for losses’
Addressing concerns over the financial implications of the Shakti scheme, which provides free bus travel to women in Karnataka, the Minister clarified that the scheme was not responsible for the financial losses incurred by the transport corporations.
Approximately 124.79 lakh passengers travel on buses operated by the four corporations every day, of whom around 74.40 lakh are women travelling free of cost under the scheme.
He said the government periodically reimburses the corporations for the expenditure incurred in providing free travel to women and, therefore, the scheme should not be viewed as a cause of their financial difficulties.
Stage-wise fare revision
Explaining the revised fare structure, Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh said ordinary bus fares operated by KSRTC, NWKRTC and KKRTC would increase by up to ₹9 for the first five stages, which account for the highest number of passengers. For express services, the maximum increase would be ₹18.
In BMTC services, fares for journeys of up to 2 km have been increased by ₹4, while journeys between 2 km and 4 km will cost ₹6 more. The maximum increase in BMTC fares will be ₹12.
The announcement, however, was marked by confusion during the press conference, with journalists repeatedly seeking clarity on the percentage-wise increase across different services as the Minister explained the revised fares on a stage-wise basis.
When reporters sought a clearer breakdown of the percentage increases, Mr. Suresh asked them to calculate the percentages themselves.

briefs.headline: Karnataka bus fare hike draws commuters’ ire; concerns over rising cost of living
briefs.deck: Commuters criticise the timing of the fare hike, citing rising household expenses, pending Shakti scheme reimbursements and the growing cost of public transport in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
The Karnataka government’s announcement to increase bus fares across State-run transport corporations has drawn the ire of commuters, who say the hike will add to the financial burden on ordinary households, particularly after the recent increases in milk and curd prices.
Commuters have expressed dissatisfaction over the timing of the decision, arguing that repeated increases in public transport fares are making daily travel increasingly expensive. Several have also questioned the rationale behind the hike, pointing out that the government is yet to clear pending reimbursements to transport corporations under schemes such as Shakti.
Using public transport tough
Prasanth Kumar, a resident of J.P. Nagar, criticised the government for repeatedly increasing public transport fares while encouraging people to use buses and the metro.
“Year after year, commuters are rewarded with fare hikes, from BMTC to the metro, even as we are encouraged to use and promote public transport. Perhaps the government should also guarantee some financial discipline instead of repeatedly passing the burden on to commuters and taxpayers. Looks like the only guarantee that keeps getting delivered is a higher cost of living for the common man,” he said.
Niranjan K., a resident of Rajajinagar, said the increase would make daily commuting more difficult, particularly for those travelling short distances. “This is totally unfair. It is becoming increasingly difficult to travel, and the fare increase is going to pinch us further. BMTC fares were already high compared to those in other metro cities, and this hike may make them even higher. Short-distance commuters will be hit harder,” he said.
He also questioned the stage-based fare calculation system followed by BMTC, arguing that passengers should not have to pay for stages they do not travel through. “Why should people have to pay from point A to point D when they board at point B and get off at point C?” he asked.
Private transport
Another commuter, Rupesh N. from HSR Layout, warned that higher bus fares could push more people towards private vehicles, defeating the objective of promoting public transport. “Now people will use more private transport, and public transport will incur losses. Due to that, fares will be increased again. Public transport should always be cheaper or subsidised. Providing free tickets for women while increasing fares significantly does not help other passengers. People will eventually shift to private vehicles, and traffic congestion will increase,” he said.
He also pointed to the Metro fare, saying Bengaluru had already become one of the most expensive cities for public transport. “Metro fares have already increased, and now bus fares are also going up. It is unfortunate for commuters,” he added.
Shakti scheme
The Shakti scheme, which provides free bus travel to women in Karnataka, has also figured prominently in the criticism, with commuters questioning the financial sustainability of the transport corporations amid reports of substantial pending government reimbursements.
“It is time for the State government to ensure better financial management and timely settlement of government dues rather than repeatedly increasing fares at the expense of passengers,” Mr. Rupesh said.
The bus fare hike comes shortly after the Karnataka government announced an increase of over ₹8 in the prices of various categories of milk and curd last week, adding to the financial burden on households.

briefs.headline: Gruha Jyothi takes largest share of guarantee spending in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
The Gruha Jyothi scheme accounts for nearly half of the expenditure incurred on the five guarantee schemes in Bengaluru, with the State government spending ₹9,625 crore on providing free electricity to eligible households since its launch in August 2023.
In Bengaluru, 38,91,445 households have availed themselves of the free electricity scheme since its inception, according to data released by the government on Wednesday. Expenditure on Gruha Jyothi accounts for 46.65% of the total ₹20,632.77 crore spent on implementing the five guarantee schemes within the limits of the five city corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority.
Recently, the power department revisited the Gruha Jyothi scheme to weed out “ineligible” and “bogus” beneficiaries and conducted a door-to-door survey. Over one lakh beneficiaries have reportedly refused to participate in the survey.
Further, Gruha Lakshmi accounts for the second-largest share of expenditure in Bengaluru. A whopping ₹5,309.52 crore (25.73%) has been spent on the scheme, according to the data. This is followed by Shakti, under which ₹3,963.61 crore (19.21%) has been spent on providing free bus travel to women in State-run transport buses.
The government will also revisit the Gruha Lakshmi scheme, for which a blueprint is being prepared for door-to-door verification. Further, the government has initiated work to issue smart cards for travel under the Shakti scheme.
Further, the government has spent ₹1,672.14 crore on Anna Bhagya, accounting for 8.1% of the total spending, while ₹62.50 crore has been spent on Yuva Nidhi, which accounts for 0.3%.
Trend in Bengaluru different
The trend in Bengaluru differs from the overall State expenditure pattern. Across Karnataka, Gruha Lakshmi accounts for the largest share of guarantee spending. A whopping ₹79,404.06 crore has been spent on Gruha Lakshmi, accounting for 51.27% of the total expenditure of ₹1,54,861.58 crore.
Meanwhile, Gruha Jyothi accounts for ₹30,521.98 crore (19.71%) of the State’s total expenditure. This is followed by Shakti at ₹22,281.94 crore (14.39%). Anna Bhagya accounts for ₹21,231.60 crore (13.71%), while ₹1,422 crore has been spent on Yuva Nidhi (0.92%) in the State.
Overall, expenditure within the Greater Bengaluru Authority limits accounts for approximately 13.3% of the State’s total spending on the five guarantee schemes.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru: Poorly maintained civic work site turns Lower Agaram Road into accident hazard
briefs.deck: Lower Agaram Road is a key route for residents of southeast Bengaluru travelling to the eastern and central parts of the city; the entire stretch is currently being white-topped, with utility works under way ahead of the project.
briefs.bodyText:
Lower Agaram Road, a key connecting stretch in the southeastern part of the city, is lined with mounds of soil and piles of debris, posing a potential hazard to commuters. The situation has persisted despite multiple directions in the past to ensure safety measures at civic work sites, prompting citizens to demand a formal standard operating procedure (SOP) for worksite management.
Lower Agaram Road is a key route for residents of southeast Bengaluru travelling to the eastern and central parts of the city. While Hosur Road was earlier the preferred route, increasing traffic congestion and ongoing Metro work over the years have led most residents to use Lower Agaram Road to reach central Bengaluru.
The entire stretch is currently being white-topped, with utility works under way ahead of the project. Excavated soil has been piled up in multiple mounds along the stretch, while large stones and sewer slabs have been left scattered haphazardly on the carriageway.
Accident-prone
While completely closing the stretch is nearly impossible given its importance for connectivity, the poor maintenance of the work site has increased the risk of accidents, particularly at night.
Vishwa Karanth, a regular commuter, said the sides of both carriageways had been dug up for over 20 days, while the scattered debris remained uncleared, slowing down traffic. “When they closed a small portion about two months ago, it used to take over 15 minutes to cover a mere 2 km along the stretch. Now, though vehicle movement is not severely affected, the risk of accidents is too high,” he said, adding it wouldn’t have been an issue if the civic body maintained the site properly by clearing debris on time and adhering to a stipulated timeline.
Karishma G.H., another commuter, said several parts of the stretch had no street lights, further increasing the risk of accidents at night. “The stretch witnesses vehicle movement even at night, including BMTC buses. Mud mounds have created several bottlenecks along the stretch, which significantly slow down traffic,” she said. “With slow-moving traffic, a lack of street lights and the cautionary signage, navigating the stretch is risky,” she added.
SOP for worksites
However, this is the same situation across several road work sites in the city.
Sujith Cariappa of the Social Amenities Association pointed out that despite repeated directions from senior officials, there were hardly any caution boards near work sites. He stressed the need for an SOP for worksite management that also specifies the timelines for completing projects.
In the past, delays have been a bone of contention between the Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP) and civic bodies, with J.C. Road being a prime example. Subsequently, the BTP began withholding permissions and directed civic bodies to carry out works in phases. However, even with phased execution, delays have persisted, while poor site management has continued to cause traffic problems. The GBA’s own data also showed that 70% of white-topping works in the city were delayed, as reported earlier by The Hindu.

briefs.headline: Four arrested for robbing man after luring him through dating app in Bengaluru’s Electronics City
briefs.deck: The complainant initially alleged that a man standing near a scooter in front of an e-commerce warehouse approached him from behind, covered his mouth with a cloth, and rendered him unconscious.
briefs.bodyText:
The Electronics City police have arrested four persons for allegedly assaulting and robbing a man after luring him through a dating application, and extorting money from him via UPI transactions. A mobile phone and a two-wheeler allegedly used in the commission of the offence have been seized. The total value of the seized property is estimated at ₹30,000.
The accused have been identified as Rishiraj Singh, 18, Vamshi, 21, Venkatesh, 25, and Darshan, 24. All four are residents of different localities in and around Electronic City.
According to the police, the complainant, a resident of Bettadasanapura Main Road, stated that he was robbed on the night of October 13 while walking along Podu Road after collecting a food parcel.
He initially alleged that a man standing near a scooter in front of an e-commerce warehouse approached him from behind, covered his mouth with a cloth, and rendered him unconscious. On regaining consciousness, he claimed to have found himself in an isolated location where five persons threatened him with a knife, assaulted him and snatched his mobile phone. The gang allegedly forced him to reveal his phone and UPI passwords, transferred money from his bank account and contacted his relatives and friends to obtain further money transfers.
The real story
However, during the investigation, the police discovered a different sequence of events. Investigators found that the complainant had been using a dating application and had chatted with an unidentified person on October 13. He had shared his location through the application and invited the person to meet him. He subsequently accompanied the person on his two-wheeler.
The police said the investigation revealed that the complainant had not been abducted, as initially alleged, and that his complaint contained a false version of the incident. However, the person he had met through the application, along with four associates, had allegedly assaulted and robbed him and forcibly obtained money through UPI transactions.
On October 18, the police apprehended three accused near Mailasandra Circle. During interrogation, they allegedly confessed to their involvement and disclosed the identity of another associate.
Acting on the information, the police arrested the fourth accused near a temple at Bettadasanapura on October 19. A two-wheeler and two mobile phones were recovered from him. He too allegedly confessed to his involvement in the crime.
All four accused were produced before a court on October 19 and remanded in judicial custody. Another associate allegedly involved in the robbery is absconding, and efforts are under way to trace him. Further investigation is in progress.

briefs.headline: 1980 Moscow Olympics gold medal stolen from home of hockey star M.M. Somaya in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: The incident, which took place in the early hours of October 28, came to light after the family returned from Kodagu district.
briefs.bodyText:
Burglars broke into the residence of former Indian hockey star M.M. Somaya at New Thippasandra in Bengaluru and took his prized 1980 Moscow Olympics gold medal, other international sporting medals, jewellery, and some cash. The incident, which took place in the early hours of October 28, came to light after the family returned from Kodagu district.
“I had left Bengaluru for my native place in Kodagu with my family on the morning of October 25. Taking advantage of the house being locked and unoccupied, two unidentified burglars have broken open the front door and entered the house around 2.34 a.m. on October 28. Around 7.15 a.m., neighbours noticed that the door of the house was open. They alerted me. Subsequently, CCTV camera footage from a neighbouring house showed two men breaking open the door and entering the premises,” he said.
Medals stolen
Mr. Somaya, a three-time Olympian who represented India in 1980, 1984 and 1988, captained the Indian Olympic hockey team at the 1988 Seoul Olympics. He was conferred the Arjuna Award in 1985.
“One of the medals stolen is India’s last Olympic Gold Medal in men’s hockey and, therefore, has immense significance not only for me personally, but also for the nation and the history of Indian sport. For me, it is an irreplaceable symbol of years of dedication, sacrifice and service to the country,” Mr. Somaya said.
Mr. Somaya’s gold medal won as part of the Indian hockey team at the 1980 Moscow Olympics, a silver medal from the 1982 Asian Games held in New Delhi, a bronze medal from the 1986 Asian Games in Seoul, and another bronze medal won at the 1982 Champions Trophy in Amsterdam, were also stolen.
The burglars also took silver cups, gold jewellery, including bangles, silver spoons, gold coins, and ₹30,000 cash. The total value of the stolen property has been estimated at ₹3.53 lakh.
Probe
The Indiranagar Police, have registered a case under Sections 331(4) and 305 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. They are examining CCTV camera footage to identify the accused and recover the stolen valuables, including the Olympic gold medal and other sporting honours. Two special teams have been formed to track down the accused, Vikram Amte, Deputy Commissioner of Police (East Division), Bengaluru City Police said.
Appeal to CM
Mr. Somaya has also written to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, seeking his intervention for a thorough and time-bound investigation into the theft of his Olympic gold medal.
Emphasising the national significance of the stolen medal, Mr. Somaya urged the Chief Minister to sensitise Bengaluru Police authorities to the exceptional national and sporting significance of the case and ensure that all necessary resources were deployed to trace and recover the medal and other stolen valuables.
“An Olympic gold medal represents far more than an individual sporting achievement; it is an honour earned for the nation on the world’s highest sporting stage,” he said, hoping that the Chief Minister’s intervention would ensure every possible effort was made to recover the medal.

stories.headline: U.S. midterm elections: An economy under pressure, political shift and the road ahead
stories.deck: Despite robust economic growth, a buoyant stock market and relatively low unemployment, rising living costs have emerged as a major political challenge for the Trump administration
stories.bodyText:

Beyond their political implications, the results raise important questions about the future direction of the world’s largest economy, particularly as American households grapple with rising living costs, persistent inflation and high borrowing expenses.
The election has highlighted a contradiction in the U.S. economy. Although real GDP expanded at an annualised rate of 3.4% in Q3 2026, a substantial section of the population remains dissatisfied with its financial circumstances. Inflation accelerated to 3.7% in September, up from 3.4% in August, largely driven by rising energy costs. stories.headline: Crude crashes below $100: Brent, WTI hit over two-month lows after midterm elections
stories.deck: Oil prices experienced a notable downturn, with Brent crude slipping below $95 and WTI declining beneath $90. This trend follows substantial losses from earlier sessions, influenced by the political shifts stemming from the US midterm elections. The election results could reshape President Donald Trump's stance towards the Iran conflict, opening doors for potential negotiations.
stories.bodyText:
Oil prices continued to ease on Thursday, with Brent crude and US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) tumbling below the $100-per-barrel threshold.
Brent slipped below the $95-per-barrel mark, while WTI fell below $90, as markets continued to react to the political fallout of the US midterm elections and the possibility of an end to the war with Iran.
Brent crude futures fell 50 cents, or 0.53%, to $94.12 a barrel, while WTI crude declined 61 cents, or 0.69%, to $87.51.
The latest movement follows Wednesday's sharp sell-off, when both benchmarks lost more than 8% and settled at their lowest levels in over two months. Brent ended the session at $94.62 a barrel, shedding $8.98 or 8.7%, while WTI settled at $88.12, down $7.97 or 8.3%. Both contracts recorded their lowest closing levels since August 31.
The market reaction came after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections, raising expectations that US President Donald Trump could face greater pressure to bring the US-Israeli war with Iran to an end.
The election outcome has also complicated Washington's options in the conflict. With Democrats taking control of the House of Representatives and the Senate, Trump could find it harder to pursue further military action. 
Two sources close to Gulf government circles told Reuters that the weakened political position gave him greater reason to pursue a negotiated settlement, making a full-scale assault on Iran less likely.
However, the possibility of a deal does not necessarily rule out further escalation. Gulf analysts said an agreement that allows Iran to claim a clear victory while leaving Trump appearing defeated could encourage recklessness rather than restraint.
Trump faces pressure as war weighs on Republicans
Trump told the Financial Times earlier this week that the US had no immediate plans to strike Iran. A day later, he acknowledged that the conflict had contributed to his party's sweeping defeat in the midterm elections.
Vice president JD Vance also questioned the decision to enter the war on Wednesday, distancing himself from it and blaming the conflict entirely for the Republicans' electoral setback.
Tehran, however, has indicated that a change in political control in Washington would not alter its position towards the US. Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement that American hostility would continue regardless of which party was in power.
There were also fresh developments in the region, with Yemen's Houthis claiming to have targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.
Qatar steps up mediation as Iran deal remains distant
Diplomatic efforts to prevent another escalation have gathered pace, with Qatar stepping up mediation following the US elections. But the prospect of an immediate breakthrough remains uncertain.
Meanwhile, regional energy flows continue to be disrupted. The United Arab Emirates is also looking at ways to reduce its reliance on the Strait of Hormuz, considering a third oil pipeline.
Separately, US oil stockpiles recorded a decline last week. The Energy Information Administration said crude inventories dropped by 865,000 barrels to 409.8 million barrels in the week ended October 30. This was sharply different from expectations in a Reuters poll, where analysts had forecast an increase of 877,000 barrels.

stories.headline: Ficci seeks exemption from LTCG for listed shares
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Industry body Ficci has sought restoration of long-term capital gains tax (LTCG) exemption on listed securities, while "appropriately" raising the securities transaction tax (STT) on delivery-based transactions to protect govt revenue.
During a pre-budget meeting with revenue secretary Arvind Shrivastava on Wednesday, the industry lobby group also suggested that the regime should be maintained for a long period -- possibly 10 years -- to provide stability and certainty to investors.
Citing withdrawals of over Rs 3 lakh crore by foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) during the year, Ficci said there was a need to review capital gains taxation to improve investment attractiveness. It said the reintroduction of LTCG tax in 2018, without withdrawal of STT, resulted in a dual levy. Since July, govt has increased short-term capital gains tax to 20%, with LTCG beyond the Rs 1.25 lakh exemption threshold pegged at 12.5%.
"Higher capital gains tax, continued STT and no forex adjustment erode post-tax equity returns," Ficci said, while seeking simplicity, fairness and stability in capital gains taxation. In recent weeks, amid demands for a review of the tax regime, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said that govt will watch the debate before taking a call in the budget.
Ficci called for exempting B2B payments liable to GST and made to GST-registered suppliers from 0.1% TDS on purchase of goods and e-commerce transactions. TDS for payments to non-GST-registered suppliers may be continued, it said.

After a muted start to the session, the index reversed course as the US mid-term election results began pointing to a landslide victory for Democratic Party. At close, tracking other global markets, sensex was up 384 points at 77,301 points, its first close above the 77K mark since late Aug.
With US President Donald Trump almost turning into a lame-duck president after the polls, US' policy decisions are expected to be more stable, felt market players. As a result, stocks rose, oil slid, rupee strengthened marginally, while gold and silver rallied.
On 
NSE

In opening trades in US, most stocks rallied, with Dow Jones Index up 2.2%, along with a 2% rally in Nasdaq Composite and a 1.6% gain in S&. While healthcare stocks rallied, defence stocks witnessed selling. 
Stocks of companies closely linked to Trump fell sharply; so did Tesla and SpaceX, majority owned by billionaire Elon Musk, the biggest contributor to Republican Party.
In the precious metals space, in early trades, gold was up 3% while silver was up nearly 5%.
Back home, the current five-session rally in the two leading indices came on the back of nearly Rs 21,000 crore (about $2.2 billion) net buying by foreign funds in the secondary market, data from NSDL and BSE showed. Later in the day, Brent crude was down 10% while Indian ADRs were up 2-3% while Gift Nifty index was up more than 2.5%, indicating a strong opening for the Indian market on Thursday. The massive slide in crude prices also affected crude derivatives on MCX with prices frozen at the 7% lower circuit.

briefs.headline: Immigration debate tone may change
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: A Democratic majority in Congress may shift the tone of the US immigration debate, but it is unlikely to bring immediate policy relief for Indian technology professionals or employers.
Experts believe a Democratic victory could help temper anti-immigrant sentiment and the political rhetoric targeting Indian technology professionals, creating a more favourable environment for skilled immigration and potentially laying the groundwork for policy changes in the longer term.
Stephen Yale-Loehr, retired professor of immigration law practice at Cornell Law School, said a change in congressional control would not immediately translate into immigration reform.
"President Trump is still president, and he controls the immigration agencies. Even if the Democrats pass positive immigration laws, President Trump can veto them. However, the Democrats can hold hearings and investigations to try to persuade the US public that immigration benefits, not hurts, the country. That way they will lay the groundwork for possible true immigration reform in 2029, assuming the Democrats control Congress then and there is a Democratic president then," he said.
David J Bier, director of Immigration Studies at Cato Institute, echoed this assessment, saying the election outcome would have almost no immediate impact on immigration policy. "It will have almost no immediate effect because Republicans still have enough votes to block most immigration bills in the Senate, and even if they didn't, Trump would veto bills that block his agenda," he said.

briefs.headline: Cabinet nod for Rs 2,814 cr plan to support critical mineral processing
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Cabinet Wednesday approved a Rs 2,814 crore scheme to boost domestic processing of lithium and nickel, reducing dependence on imports of critical minerals.
PM Narendra Modi said India cannot afford to depend on other countries for processing such materials. The scheme would encourage domestic investment and secure future supplies, he wrote on X.
Union ministry of mines said processing of critical minerals was concentrated in a few global locations. The scheme aims to develop domestic processing capabilities, promote value addition and reduce import dependence by supporting processing facilities.
It targets processing lithium and nickel ores or intermediary products into high-purity compounds. Cobalt is expected to be recovered as a by-product of nickel production. To be implemented until FY31, the scheme will provide a capital subsidy of 30% of eligible investment for four plants: two lithium processing plants with minimum capacity of 30,000 tonnes each and two nickel plants with minimum capacity of 50,000 tonnes each.
The support will be capped at Rs 500 crore per lithium beneficiary and Rs 900 crore per nickel beneficiary.

briefs.headline: India secures $400-bn investment commitments in renewables; ALMM review in 15 days

India has secured preliminary investment commitments worth $400 billion across the renewable energy sector, including green hydrogen, energy storage and transmission, among others, Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi said on Wednesday.
Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo, Mr. Joshi said the commitments were made during a CEO roundtable involving global investors and fund managers.

The minister said overseas investors had expressed confidence in India’s investment climate. “I also met the Canadian Investment Fund – they are one of the biggest funds. They also said this (India) was the safest place for investment,” he said.
ALMM extension decision in 10-15 days
Separately, the government will consult industry stakeholders over the next 10-15 days before deciding whether to extend the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) framework, Mr. Joshi said.
The framework, which mandates the use of domestically approved solar module manufacturers for specified projects, was last extended in July until December 31 for solar PV cells.
He said India’s solar cell manufacturing capacity currently stood at 41 GW, while manufacturers had committed to adding another 70 GW by the end of the year.
Acknowledging divergent views within the industry on extending the ALMM framework, he said the government would hear both sides before taking a decision.

briefs.headline: Centre earmarks ₹2,814 crore to boost lithium, nickel processing
briefs.deck: In a social media post, Union Coal and Mines Minister G. Kishan Reddy stated the scheme would help strengthen domestic capabilities, boost manufacturing and reduce dependence on imports.
briefs.bodyText:
The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a ₹2,814-crore capital expenditure support scheme to establish domestic processing facilities for lithium and nickel, seeking to strengthen India’s critical mineral ecosystem and reduce import dependence. The scheme will remain in force for five years.
India’s domestic beneficiation and processing infrastructure for critical minerals remains limited, with commercial-scale operations constrained by high capital requirements, limited access to suitable technologies and inadequate availability of raw materials, the government said in a statement.
Union Minister for Coal and Mines G. Kishan Reddy said the scheme would strengthen domestic capabilities, boost manufacturing and reduce dependence on imports.
“It will benefit key sectors such as electronics, semiconductors, batteries, defence, heavy equipment and machinery, while supporting industries across the manufacturing value chain that utilise critical minerals,” he said in a social media post.
Subsidy structure
Under the scheme, the government will provide a capital subsidy of 30% of the investment required to establish four critical mineral processing plants — two each for lithium and nickel.
The minimum processing capacity will be 30,000 tonnes (30 kt) each for lithium and 50,000 tonnes (50 kt) each for nickel.
The subsidy will be capped at ₹500 crore per beneficiary for lithium projects and ₹900 crore per beneficiary for nickel facilities.
The four beneficiaries will be selected through a least-cost bidding process, with preference given to technically qualified applicants seeking the lowest capital expenditure support. Incentives will be disbursed in three tranches.
Industry welcomes move
Industry body the Federation of Indian Mineral Industries (FIMI) welcomed the initiative, saying it could encourage fresh investments, increase domestic value addition and strengthen supply chains for battery manufacturing and other strategic industries.
However, it said that securing adequate raw materials would be critical to the scheme’s success.
“Ensuring a reliable supply of raw material through domestic mining and overseas sourcing will be equally important for the success of these processing facilities,” the industry body told The Hindu.
It also underlined the need to develop the entire value chain, from mining to processing and refining, to strengthen India’s long-term mineral security.

briefs.headline: Mercedes-Benz Group AG to scale up technology, components sourcing from India; launches electric GLC starting ₹78.5 lakh
briefs.bodyText:
India will play an important role in Mercedes-Benz Group AG’s global business as the company would source more technology and components from India for it’s global operations before exporting vehicles from the country, Ola Kallenius, Mercedes-Benz’s Group AG Chairman of the Board of Management, said in a select interaction.
“We are building strong tech and supply relationships in India, not just for India, also for the rest of the world. So we can, export out of India on a component basis before a full vehicle,” he said.
“And these tech partnerships and supply partnerships are going from strength to strength. And the fact that we have the biggest R&D center outside of Germany here in Bengaluru, we also have a very competent production setup since more than 30 years,” he stated.
“We have all the ingredients. So this is not a one dimensional play. India in the Mercedes world is a 360 degree play,” he emphasised.
Asked when the company would export vehicles from India, he said, “I am an India believer and certainly an India optimist. I think that is more a question of when as opposed to a question of if.”
“But I want to make clear we have not made such a decision at this point in time,” he said, adding the company would wait for volumes to grow in India before embarking on exports.
“So, the first step on the further journey is what organic growth can we have from this point forward. We believe, based upon projections around GDP growth, what we think that the market in India can be in the next five, six, seven years, that we can significantly grow from that number upwards,” he added.
He said R& D in India will play a bigger role and the company would build stronger supply relationships to source components.
The company sees energy transition as a reality and being the inventor of automobiles and as an incumbent, it is strengthening it’s capabilities in newer fuels.
“The automotive industry is in transition. It’s in transformation, I would say disruption. What’s driving the disruption is the road to zero emissions and we don’t have to discuss the destination. The destination is zero emission. It’s just a question of how long it takes,” he said.
“We are reinventing the original invention. So there’s always turbulence when you go through a transformation of that magnitude,” he said adding many new entrants will come in and they of course will go for electric mobility, but the legacy players too will be in the race to succeed.
“If you’re an incumbent, you don’t cut off the leg that you stand on right now and you build a new one. So you have to manage a transition that it’s not like with smartphones,” he stated.
“The destination is zero emission, that’s where we are going,” he emphasised.
Stating that the company has taken diesel to EU7 standards, he said diesel engines will stay in the portfolio for the foreseeable future.
The company on Wednesday announced a fresh investment of ₹200 crore in India, taking the total investment to ₹3,200 crore and introduced its electric GLC SUV at a starting price of ₹78.5 lakh.
The SUV has 711 kms range in one charge and 300 kms of energy can be charged in 10 minutes.
Over 1,000 bookings had been received even before the announcement of price, indicating the demand for EVs in India, the company said.
