stories.headline: 'God help you': Shastri as Virat Kohli breaks Sachin Tendulkar's record
stories.deck: Virat Kohli made batting look easy in India's first ODI against New Zealand in Auckland on Wednesday. The star batter scored 74 runs off 51 balls to help India win the match by five wickets (DLS) and take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series. India had to chase a revised target of 143 runs in 32 overs. Kohli made sure there was no late drama as India reached the target in just 22.4 overs. Kohli…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
Virat Kohli
 made batting look easy in India's first ODI against New Zealand in Auckland on Wednesday. The star batter scored 74 runs off 51 balls to help India win the match by five wickets (DLS) and take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series.
India had to chase a revised target of 143 runs in 32 overs. Kohli made sure there was no late drama as India reached the target in just 22.4 overs.
Kohli hit 13 fours and a six during his innings. His shots through the covers and pulls were among the highlights of his knock.
Former India head coach Ravi Shastri was full of praise for Kohli. He said the 74-run innings was as valuable as a century because of the conditions in which it was played.
"A 70 in conditions like these is worth a hundred. He never got ahead of himself throughout the innings. And when he stays in fourth gear like this, then God help you. When the youngsters in the dressing room watch him and how he still gets angry at getting out at 38, they'll understand they have work to do," Ravi Shastri said on Sony Sports.
Shastri also spoke about the support Kohli gave captain Shubman Gill during the chase. 
According to him, Kohli's ability to take quick singles kept the New Zealand bowlers under pressure.
"He also took a lot of pressure off Shubman Gill at the other end. He gets off strike so quickly that the pressure is on the bowler at all times. I've seen him for all those years and I can't tell you if he has batted better."
Kohli leaves Sachin behind in ODI chases
Kohli's innings also helped him break another major record. He went past Sachin Tendulkar to become the highest run-scorer in ODI run chases. Sachin had scored 8,720 runs in 242 innings while batting second in ODIs. His record included 17 centuries and 52 half-centuries at an average of 42.33.
Kohli has now scored 8,741 runs in 169 innings in ODI chases. He has done so at an average of 66.21 and a strike rate of 95.03. His tally includes 30 centuries and 46 half-centuries.
His record is even better when India win while chasing. Kohli has scored 6,477 runs in 108 innings in successful ODI chases. His average is 89.95 and his strike rate is over 98. He has scored 25 centuries and 30 half-centuries, with 183 being his highest score.
Kohli matches Ponting's record against New Zealand
There was another record for Kohli in the first ODI. He equalled former Australia captain Ricky Ponting's record for the most runs against New Zealand in ODI cricket.
Both Kohli and Ponting have scored 1,971 runs against New Zealand.
Kohli has reached this total in 37 innings at an average of 57.97 and a strike rate of 97.86. He has seven centuries and 11 half-centuries against the Black Caps.
Ponting scored the same number of runs in 50 innings across 51 matches. His average was 45.83, with six centuries and 12 half-centuries.
Kohli's latest performance added two more major records to his name and helped India start the ODI series with a win.

stories.headline: Ranji Trophy: Father played alongside Kapil Dev, son Jayant Goyat bags maiden fifer, wants to wear India colours
stories.deck: Services pacer Jayant Goyat's maiden five-wicket haul, in his 12th first-class match, has strengthened his belief in an India dream. The 21-year-old from Bhiwani, whose father was part of Haryana's Ranji Trophy squad during Kapil Dev's last season, discusses his journey from India Under-19 cricket, the challenges of bowling on Palam's flat surfaces and the support that keeps him going.
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: "Desh ke liye khelne ke liye jigra chahiye hota hai (It takes guts to play for the country)," Jayant Goyat told this reporter on the sidelines of Day 2 of the ongoing 
Ranji Trophy
 match between Delhi and Services at the Air Force Complex Ground in Palam.
The conversation revolved around the challenges of bowling on a Palam pitch, where conditions are often either flat or favour spin, and how a 21-year-old fast bowler keeps his India ambition alive while operating in such conditions.
On Day 3, Goyat registered his maiden five-wicket haul in his 12th first-class appearance for Services. His early breakthroughs on Wednesday helped Services fight back in the game.
"It is a very good feeling. It is my first fifer. The wicket is slow and flat, so I had to put in extra effort. I did that and got the results," he told reporters.
It was a double delight for the six-foot-four-inch-tall pacer, who hails from Haryana's Bhiwani district. The 21-year-old, who joined the Air Force through the Agniveer scheme, has received an extension after the Union Cabinet approved an additional two-year engagement period for 75% of Agniveers. The lanky seamer, who has played all his age-group cricket for Haryana, just smiled when a handful of reporters broke the news to him.
Services seamer Jayant Goyat (Photo: Pratyush Raj)
Services head coach AP Singh, a Lieutenant Colonel in the Indian Army, lauded Goyat and said he sees a lot of potential in the youngster.
"Absolutely, he is an exciting talent, and we are in the process of grooming him for the next level. He has age on his side, he is talented, and he is bowling very well. This was his first five-wicket haul today in a very big game. He is an exciting talent," said the coach.
"He bowled brilliantly today. That is what we had discussed in the team meeting. All they need to do on these wickets is bowl in good areas and not go searching for wickets. Being a youngster full of enthusiasm, there is a tendency to go for wickets. That is where you leak runs and don't even get a wicket," added Singh.
My father took me to cricket. He also played Ranji Trophy for Haryana. He was a fast bowler and was part of the squad during Kapil Dev's last season.
Jayant Goyat
Jayant's five-wicket haul was a significant step in that learning process, with the coach pointing out how the youngster had applied the lessons discussed in the team meeting.
"Today's five-wicket haul was a big learning experience for him. In fact, he categorically told me that what we discussed in the team meeting had worked for him. Just bowl in good areas and good lengths, and you will get wickets," said Singh.
Although Bhiwani is known for producing athletes in combat sports, Goyat grew up in a cricket-loving family. His father, Dr Wazir Singh Goyat, was part of the Haryana Ranji Trophy team during 
Kapil Dev
's last season. Although he never got the opportunity to make his debut, Goyat Sr. never stopped his son from pursuing his dream. He is currently working as a professor of physical education at Maharaja Neempal Singh Government College in Bhiwani.
"My father took me to cricket. He also played Ranji Trophy for Haryana. He was a fast bowler and was part of the squad during Kapil Dev's last season," Goyat said.
"I played for India Under-19 last season and was on standby for the World Cup (2024). I got to know [about Services]. I knew local guys in Services. I gave a trial and got selected," he added.
Jayant Goyat with his father Wazir Singh Goyat. (Special Arrangement)
Goyat recollected his father's unwavering support during the time he was playing for India Under-19 and was not able to perform well.
"My father never pushed me to play cricket. He let me do what I wanted. I wanted to play cricket. He supported me a lot. I can't even say how much. Even when I was down a lot, he gave me a lot of moral support," he said.
"When I played India Under-19, I wasn't performing for three-four matches on the trot for Haryana. I said one time that I was quitting cricket. He pushed me, and then my team started performing well. Depending on his mood, he motivates me in different ways. He motivated me then by giving me my favourite food," added Goyat with a smile.
Goyat, who has played all his cricket as a batting all-rounder, idolises legendary South African all-rounder Jacques Kallis and has batted in the top order. He says he is training hard to add a few yards to his bowling.
He is always happy and creates a good environment in the team. He doesn't get bogged down easily. Attitude is a very big thing, and that is what we look for in players.
AP Singh | Services head coach
"My natural length is back of a length. I do look to hit the deck. I do think I can add speed. At Under-19, I bowled at 134-135 kmph. It is about the training regime to add speed. I work with the Services S&C. The main thing is about strength. It is about strengthening the lower body. The more I do strength training, the better it is," he said.
Meanwhile, Services coach showered praise on Jayant's attitude, describing him as someone who brings positivity into the dressing room and does not get weighed down by setbacks.
"As far as I have seen, he is a jolly good fellow. He is always happy and creates a good environment in the team. He doesn't get bogged down easily. Attitude is a very big thing, and that is what we look for in players. That is how players grow and perform well at this stage."

stories.headline: PSG, Barca turn on the magic, United posts win
stories.deck: PSG was ruthless, with Joao Neves, Desire Doue, Senny Mayulu and Fabian Ruiz all striking in eight first-half minutes as the French outfit set a record for the fastest four goals scored in a match in Europe’s elite club competition
stories.bodyText:
Manchester United fought back from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) to hand beleaguered manager Michael Carrick a reprieve, while holder Paris Saint-Germain continued its perfect start in the competition by hitting Villarreal for six.
Raphinha struck twice to propel Barcelona to a 3-0 win over visitor Aston Villa. Barcelona took an early lead through Lamine Yamal before Raphinha continued his fine goalscoring form.
Looking set for another abject defeat when two behind within 18 minutes through a smart Mathias Soule finish and Donyell Malen’s penalty, United staged a thrilling comeback in the second half to turn a poisonous atmosphere at Old Trafford to one of joy. Matheus Cunha, who was sent off in stoppage time, saved the day for United with a brace in three minutes with the final whistle nearing, sparking wild celebrations in the stands.
PSG was ruthless, with Joao Neves, Desire Doue, Senny Mayulu and Fabian Ruiz all striking in eight first-half minutes as the French outfit set a record for the fastest four goals scored in a match in Europe’s elite club competition. Further strikes from Ruiz and teenager David Boly rounded off a stellar performance.
Bayern Munich, missing a host of stars, saw off Atletico Madrid 2-0 to move into the top eight positions.

stories.headline: Indian shooters miss medal targets
stories.deck: The 10m air rifle mixed team pair of Sonam Uttam Maskar and Himanshu Dhillon failed to qualify for the four-team final, finishing seventh with an aggregate of 632.4. Sonam shot 316.6, while Himanshu returned 315.8
stories.bodyText:
Indian shooters endured another disappointing day at the ISSF World Championships in Doha on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), failing to compete for medals in both the 10m air rifle mixed team and 25m rapid fire pistol events.
The 10m air rifle mixed team pair of Sonam Uttam Maskar and Himanshu Dhillon failed to qualify for the four-team final, finishing seventh with an aggregate of 632.4. Sonam shot 316.6, while Himanshu returned 315.8.
The other Indian pair, Shambhavi Kshirsagar and Parth Mane, was disqualified after the former fell foul of the ISSF rules pertaining to apparel and equipment.
It was Shambhavi’s second disqualification in a major competition in five months for a similar violation. She had also been disqualified at the ISSF Junior World Championships in Suhl in June.
India’s medal hopes also fizzled out in the 25m rapid fire pistol event, with none of the three shooters managing to make the eight-shooter final.
On Tuesday, the Indian troika of Ravinder Singh, Saurabh Chaudhary and Amanpreet Singh clinched the team gold in men’s 50m pistol competition.
Ravinder also won the silver in individual competition of the event that is not on the Olympic roster.

briefs.headline: 'That's for my girlfriend': Arshdeep reveals romantic reason behind unique celebration
briefs.deck: Arshdeep Singh delighted fans by showcasing a special dance dedicated to his girlfriend Samreen Kaur after claiming a wicket. He shared that these dance moves are a mood booster during tough times. His outstanding four-wicket haul was pivotal for India's bowling prowess, while Virat Kohli's steady batting led India to a five-wicket victory post-rain delay, putting them in the lead in their ODI…
briefs.bodyText:
Arshdeep Singh had a special reason to break into a dance after taking a wicket against New Zealand in the first ODI. The Indian pacer revealed that his unique on-field celebration was dedicated to his girlfriend, actor-model Samreen Kaur. The gesture, he explained, was inspired by dance steps the couple share to lift each other's spirits.
Speaking during the innings interval on Sony Sports, Arshdeep opened up about the personal meaning behind the celebration.
"That's for my girlfriend. We do these dance steps when we're out walking or something like that. Whenever the mood is a little low, we cheer each other up with that celebration. So this was for her," he said.
Arshdeep shines with four-wicket haul
The celebration came after Arshdeep dismissed New Zealand all-rounder Kyle Jamieson, who was caught by Virat Kohli. The left-arm pacer finished with figures of 4/70 in his 10 overs, leading India's bowling attack.
Arshdeep's performance helped India bowl New Zealand out for 185 in 40.2 overs at Eden Park. Gurnoor Brar claimed three wickets, while Anshul Kamboj picked up two.
Virat Kohli guides India to victory
In reply, India overcame an early setback after Rohit Sharma fell for a duck. 
Virat Kohli anchored the chase with a fluent 74 off 51 balls, while captain Shubman Gill contributed 37. The duo added 113 runs for the second wicket to put India in a commanding position.
Rain interruptions revised India's target to 143 in 32 overs under the DLS method. The visitors reached 143/5 in 22.4 overs to seal a five-wicket victory with 56 balls to spare.
The win gave India a 1-0 lead in the three-match ODI series. While Arshdeep's four-wicket haul played a crucial role in the victory, his heartfelt celebration added a personal touch to an impressive outing.

briefs.headline: History! Tanvi Patri becomes first Indian woman to reach Youth Olympic badminton final
briefs.deck: Tanvi Patri has made history by reaching the badminton final at the Youth Olympic Games in Buenos Aires. She defeated Japan's Yuzuno Watanabe in a challenging three-game semifinal match. Previously, only three Indian players had attained similar success in this competition. Tanvi has previously won prestigious titles at the Badminton Asia U-17 Championships as well.
briefs.bodyText:
India's Tanvi Patri scripted history on Wednesday by becoming the first Indian woman to reach the 
badminton
 final at the Youth Olympic Games. The 15-year-old defeated Japan's Yuzuno Watanabe 21-14, 11-21, 21-19 in a thrilling three-game semifinal in Buenos Aires. The Odisha shuttler showed great fighting spirit to overcome her opponent and move within one win of a historic gold medal.
Tanvi had to work hard for the victory after Watanabe bounced back strongly in the second game. However, the Indian kept her calm in the deciding game and came up with some attacking shots to seal the contest. The victory was also a sweet revenge for Tanvi, who had lost to Watanabe 21-14, 21-10 in their previous meeting in Thailand.
Before her, only three Indian shuttlers - HS Prannoy, Lakshya Sen and Aditya Joshi - had reached the badminton semifinals at the competition.
Prannoy won silver at the inaugural Youth Olympic Games in Singapore in 2010. Lakshya also finished with a silver medal at the 2018 edition in Buenos Aires. Aditya, meanwhile, reached the boys' singles semifinals in 2014 but returned without a medal.
Tanvi has already made a name for herself in junior badminton. She earlier won the girls' singles U-17 title at the Badminton Asia U-17 and U-15 Championships in Chengdu, becoming the first Indian shuttler to win both continental titles.
Now, the 15-year-old has a chance to create another piece of history. One more victory will give her a Youth Olympic gold medal and make her achievement even more special.

briefs.headline: Sports journalist Bhasi Malaparamba no more
briefs.deck: He reported eight World Cups, between 1982 and 2010, as well as the European Championship in 2008
briefs.bodyText:
Bhasi Malaparamba, sports journalist and novelist, passed away, aged 85. Though he was an engineer by profession and he worked in the PWD, he was better known for his coverage of several football World Cups as a freelance journalist.
He reported eight World Cups, between 1982 and 2010, as well as the European Championship in 2008. He also published several novels in Malayalam. He was a competitive footballer who represented Kozhikode district.
Bhasi’s was a friendly presence in the sporting and cultural spheres of Kozhikode. Until he fell, he would attend most of the football matches held in the city, even when he was not on a reporting assignment.
Bhasi’s contribution to Malayalam sports journalism as a knowledgeable football writer was significant, especially in the pre-Internet era.

Each player and team will face the other three in their group over the first six days, with the top two advancing to semifinals.

briefs.headline: Virat Kohli creates history! Becomes first to average 50-plus in all SENA countries
briefs.deck: Virat Kohli has reached a remarkable achievement by maintaining an average above 50 across all four SENA nations. In the first ODI against New Zealand, he contributed 74 runs, leading India to a decisive victory. Moreover, he surpassed Sachin Tendulkar to become the highest run-scorer in ODI chases, matched Ricky Ponting's run tally versus New Zealand, and became the first player to hit 13,000…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
Virat Kohli
 added another landmark to his extraordinary ODI career on Wednesday, becoming the first batter in the history of the format to maintain an average of 50 or more in all four SENA countries — South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.
The India batting stalwart achieved the feat during the first ODI against New Zealand at Auckland, where he produced an authoritative 74 off just 51 balls. His innings, studded with 13 fours and a six, came at a strike rate of over 145 and helped India negotiate a rain-curtailed chase with ease.
Kohli's average in New Zealand stood at 49.66 before the match. His latest knock took it to 51.53, completing a unique set of 50-plus averages across the four countries. He now averages 76.38 in South Africa, 51.48 in England, 51.53 in New Zealand and 50.03 in Australia.
The milestone underlines Kohli's remarkable consistency in conditions traditionally regarded as challenging for visiting batters. He has scored 993 runs in South Africa, 1,493 in England, 670 in New Zealand and 1,401 in Australia.
Kohli surpasses Tendulkar as leading ODI run-scorer in chases
The Auckland innings also saw 
Kohli move past another iconic record held by Sachin Tendulkar
. He became the highest run-scorer in ODI run-chases, taking his tally to 8,741 runs and going past Tendulkar's 8,720.
Kohli has accumulated those runs in 180 matches and 169 innings at an average of 66.21 and a strike rate of 95.03, with 30 centuries and 46 half-centuries.
His numbers in successful chases are even more striking. The former India captain has scored 6,477 runs in 114 matches and 108 innings at an average of 89.95 and a strike rate above 98. That tally includes 25 centuries and 30 fifties, with a highest score of 183.
The record further reinforces Kohli's reputation as one of the most prolific batters in ODI chases, particularly when India are pursuing a target.
Equals Ricky Ponting's record against New Zealand
Kohli also drew level with Australian great Ricky Ponting for the most ODI runs against New Zealand. Both batters now have 1,971 runs against the Black Caps.
Kohli has reached the mark in 37 innings at an average of 57.97 and a strike rate of 97.86, with seven centuries and 11 half-centuries. Ponting took 50 innings across 51 matches to score the same number of runs, averaging 45.83, with six centuries and 12 fifties.
The India batter also became the first player to reach 13,000 ODI runs while batting at No. 3. He has scored 13,062 runs in 254 matches and 251 innings at the position, averaging 61.61. His tally includes 48 centuries and 70 half-centuries, with a best score of 183.
Kohli's rich run continues after Test retirement
Kohli's latest milestone comes amid an impressive run in the 50-over format. Since retiring from Test cricket, he has scored 1,002 runs in 16 ODIs at an average of 77.07, including four centuries and six half-centuries.
He has also been among the leading performers in ODIs this year. In 10 matches, Kohli has accumulated 626 runs at an average of 69.55 and a strike rate of 120.61. The tally features two centuries and four fifties, with a highest score of 139 not out.
Arshdeep, Kamboj lead India's bowling effort in Auckland
Kohli's innings was among the major highlights of India's five-wicket victory
 in the rain-affected series opener at Auckland.
After being put under pressure by India's bowlers, New Zealand were bowled out for 185. Arshdeep Singh spearheaded the attack with an impressive four-wicket haul, while Gurnoor Brar claimed three wickets for 44 runs in 9.2 overs. Anshul Kamboj chipped in with two wickets, conceding just 22 runs in his 10 overs.
India were set a revised target of 143 in 32 overs under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method after rain interruptions. Kohli's brisk 74 ensured the chase remained on course, as India reached the target comfortably to take an early lead in the series.

briefs.headline: Sonu and Ajith push Tamil Nadu closer to victory against Chandigarh
briefs.deck: Four-wicket hauls from both bowlers help visitors bundle out hosts for 94 in 1st innings, before pinning them to 189 for seven in their second essay
briefs.bodyText:
Just before taking the field on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), the entire Tamil Nadu unit, including the support staff, gathered in a huddle. Head coach Yo Mahesh yelled: “What do we have?” The players roared: “Freedom!”
“How do we do it?” came the next question. “Together!” the group roared.
Those two words — freedom and togetherness — dictated the third day’s play as TN tightened its grip on its Ranji Trophy Elite Group D fourth-round clash against Chandigarh at the Sector-16 Ground in Chandigarh.
The visitor needed just 17.3 overs in the morning session to dismiss the host for 94 in its first innings.
Following on, Chandigarh reached 189 for seven at stumps, still trailing by 288 runs and staring at an innings defeat.
The host began its second essay with greater composure. Openers Nehal Pajni and Arjun Azad (60, 90b, 8x4, 1x6) rotated the strike and took the score past 50 before skipper R. Sai Kishore broke the 73-run stand, thanks to a stunning effort at forward short-leg by G. Ajitesh just before lunch.
With the surface easing out in the afternoon, Manan Vohra (59, 72b, 11x4) and Arjun looked assured, adding 82 for the second wicket. However, a moment of madness changed the course of the innings. Arjun danced down the track to left-arm spinner S. Ajith Ram, only to be stumped, opening the gates for the visitor.
The wickets then came in a hurry. Saravana Kumar trapped Manan in front, while Ajith removed Akshit Rana and Bhagmender Lather. Sai Kishore dismissed Chiragvir Dhindsa before Ajith ended Arjit Pannu’s stubborn 57-ball, nine-run resistance.
Earlier, with the festivities just around the corner, the procession began in the second over of the morning, with medium-pacer Sonu Yadav leading the way.
He flattened overnight batter Arjit’s stumps with a full-length delivery before sending Bhagmender’s timber cartwheeling.
Chiragvir then departed following a needless run-out, before Sonu disturbed Nikhil Sharma’s furniture as Chandigarh slipped to 76 for seven.
Saravana Kumar dismissed Akshit Rana and sent Jagjit Singh’s stumps for a morning walk. Fittingly, Sonu returned to end the host’s misery, dismissing Nishunk Birla.

briefs.headline: Kamboj tailor-made for these conditions: Skipper Gill
briefs.deck: “Anshul is the kind of a bowler. I think he’s tailor-made for these conditions, always nippy, trying to seam the ball, and good with the old ball,” Shubman Gill said
briefs.bodyText:
India captain Shubman Gill was delighted to see Anshul Kamboj’s excellent effort in the first ODI against New Zealand in Auckland on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), saying the pacer is “tailor-made” for the Antipodean conditions.
“Anshul is the kind of a bowler. I think he’s tailor-made for these conditions, always nippy, trying to seam the ball, and good with the old ball,” Gill told the broadcaster during the post-match presentation.
“We felt when there’s not much happening from the wicket, he can create that extra bounce and with his pace and the way both of them bowled tonight was really magnificent to watch,” he said.
“We were very good with the bowling and our fielding was also really good. That run out by Rohit bhai, I think changed the momentum of the game,” Gill said.
“It was really that partnership as even in India also those two batted really well. Overall, a very good team performance for us”.

briefs.headline: Kimi Antonelli - A new face for a new era
briefs.deck: Mercedes team boss punted on the Italian and backed him through a bruising rookie year, a barrage of doubts and a few departing sponsors. But he never once wavered in his belief. The youngest champion in F1 history has repaid that faith, and silenced the critics along the way
briefs.bodyText:
Some nights, a whole country stops and looks at glowing screens, big and small. When people speak of the moon landing, they remember where they were. After this weekend, Italy will remember where it was too. A nation that lives and breathes motorsport sat glued to the television as Kimi Antonelli became the youngest champion in Formula One history.
He is not the first Italian to wear the crown, but he is the first to win it in front of a nation watching together. Alberto Ascari, the last Italian champion, was crowned on August 23, 1953, a few months before the country’s first nationwide television broadcast on January 3, 1954.
